text: Intro

A school burned on a Tuesday night. The whole district said somebody set it on fire. The Paris Emergency Switchboard sent the crime unit a year of its calls, alarms and patrols. One call came in before the first witness saw the fire.

The science wing of College Jean Moulin burned on the evening of 14 October. Nobody was hurt. Everybody has a theory.

You have a year of the Paris Emergency Switchboard's log and 4 words of SQL.
One table, `dispatch_log`: a year of the Paris Emergency Switchboard's log.
Which call reported the school fire before the first witness saw it?
OCTOBER 15, 2025
Chief Forensics Reporter
Criminal Fire Destroys Science Wing at College Jean Moulin
Flames Seen From the Street at 21:12. Neighbours Insist It Was Deliberate

The science wing of College Jean Moulin burned last night. Nobody was hurt. A passer-by saw flames at 21:12, and the firefighters were there a minute later. By the next morning the district said somebody started it on purpose. There was a chemistry store, and no system to put out a fire.

The police have no suspects and one file. It holds a year of calls from the Paris Emergency Switchboard. Detectives have to find one night in a year of calls. Then they have to find the time of that call.
"One call reached us 14 minutes before anyone on the street saw a flame."
A year at the Paris Emergency Switchboard: every call, sighting, alarm panel, patrol and fire engine in Paris, with the day and the hour it was written down.
Open the *Archive*
The Paris Emergency Switchboard logged a year of emergency calls in Paris.
Type `SELECT * FROM dispatch_log` and Run it. When the rows are there, press Verify. `SELECT *` asks for every column, and `FROM` names the table.
Every row of the year, with all 8 columns.
2,400 rows in a year. Calls, witnesses, alarms, patrols.
The *Night*
The fire was on 14 October.
Keep only the rows of that day, `2025-10-14`, from `dispatch_log`. `WHERE` keeps the rows where a condition is true. Write the column, `=`, then the value in single quotes.
16 rows: everything logged that day.
Too *Early*
The first witness saw the school's flames at 21:12. One call about the fire came in before that.
Find that call in `dispatch_log` and return its row. `AND` adds a second condition to a `WHERE`.
One row: the early call.
20:58. 14 minutes before the first witness saw the fire.
Flames at 21:12 → `dispatch_log` → one school fire call before it: 20:58, `LINE 4417`.
